The Genoese ratio was customary and invariant until the late thirteenth century. The agent's word prevails as trustee on the amount of capital, 'li-annahu mudda'a 'alayhi wa-huwa amin', and on transgression (Mudawwana 3, 661); his oath is stated where the profit share is disputed (Muw 2054); a loss claimed after he had admitted the capital intact needs 'amr yu'rafu bihi qawluhu' (Muw 2053). No oath is stated for a loss claim in what was read. READ WITH mudaraba_alloc VF1: one Islamic datum. PREVIOUS NOTE: REPLACED 2026-10-11 by LM-R0059. claimant-oath (second instance; value added 2026-10-11, records/RULINGS-comanda-adjudications-2026-10-11.md, ruling 2). Mabsut 22, 27: 'wa-ra's al-mal amana fi yad al-mudarib ka'l-wadi'a ... wa-yuqbal qawl al-mudarib fihi li-kawnihi aminan ... fa-in ikhtalafa fi miqdar ra's al-mal ... fa'l-qawl qawl al-mudarib ma'a yaminihi li-annahu huwa al-qabid' - the capital is a trust in his hands like a deposit, his word is accepted because he is a trustee, and in a dispute over the amount of capital his word prevails WITH HIS OATH. Mabsut 22, 51: 'li-annahu amin fima fi yadihi min al-mal fa-yakun maqbul al-qawl fihi ka'l-wakil bi'l-bay' idha qala bi'tu wa-qabadtu al-thaman wa-halaka fi yadi yuqbal qawluhu' - he is a trustee over the property in his hands and his word is accepted, like the sales agent who says the price perished in his hand. TWO LIMITS, RECORDED: the oath is stated for the trustee's accepted word (p. 27, a dispute over the amount of capital), not repeated in the loss passage (p. 51); and whether the investor's bayyina rebuts a loss claim is not stated in the passages read. Previously .NR because no held source described the mode. LIMIT DISCHARGED 2026-10-11 (v): Mabsut 22, 108 applies the oath to the trustee's discharge from liability for the capital - 'wa-yustahlaf al-mudarib bi'llah ma istahlakaha wa-la dayya'aha li-anna al-mudarib amin fi ra's al-mal wa'l-qawl qawl al-amin ma'a al-yamin fi bara'atihi 'an al-daman' (he is made to swear by God that he neither consumed it nor lost it through neglect, because he is a trustee over the capital and the trustee's word with his oath prevails in his discharge from liability). The context is a dispute over whether the capital was returned; the ground stated is general. The second limit (rebuttal by the investor's bayyina) stands: p. 94 gives the bayyina to the investor who alleges a cause of liability, there a loan, not a loss through fault. See LM-0762 (VF2).
